messages.content:
Kaggle has acknowledged that the dataset cache was unstable in some regions and that fixes were deployed. We want to add one data point: on our side the problem was not gone this morning.

What we see

  • We run the same notebook with the same inputs every day; the model weights are already stored in Kaggle Models.
  • Until about Oct 19, loading took a few minutes.
  • This morning (Oct 24), two of our runs started at the same time, and both took over an hour just to read the model files.
  • Two of our submissions this week scored exactly 0.00, although the interactive runs of the same versions were healthy.

We wrote to Kaggle support about the zero scores. They did not answer the question and directed us to the forum, so we are raising it here.

What has helped us, in line with what other participants found

  • Keep at least one game making cheap moves until the model server reports healthy, so the gateway does not close the run for inactivity.
  • Allow much longer for the server to start than the defaults assume, in the notebook and in the agent's give-up timers.
  • Restart the server process if it dies while loading.
  • Before submitting, check in the interactive run's log that the server came up and games made moves.

None of this helps if a rerun stops on a platform-side system error, which several teams report as well.

Questions for the hosts

  1. Is the fix expected to cover the scored reruns too, and when will it be safe to rely on normal loading times again?
  2. Will submissions that failed because of the scoring environment be re-scored or excluded, or will the daily slot be returned?
  3. Could scored reruns report a minimal status line (server started, games and actions run, why the run ended), so teams can tell a platform failure from their own bug?

Hope this saves someone a submission.
